forecaster_note: Surf Guru read: the week opens on scraps and finishes with the best swell in a fortnight — plan around that. Today is leftovers: a 2.3ft @ 7s SSE windswell (158°) doing most of the work with a thin 0.7ft @ 15s SE groundswell underneath, total energy only ~34 kJ. Thigh-to-waist stuff. What saves it is a proper WNW offshore (303°, 12 kph gusting 26) grooming everything clean — pretty, but underpowered. Long Reef and Curl Curl hold the most size; Dee Why and Manly sit soft. Tomorrow (Wed) is the throwaway: energy collapses to ~10 kJ and the W/SW blows 17–25 kph gusting 39 by the afternoon. Then the weekend delivers. Saturday a 5.7ft @ 10s S pulse (~425 kJ) fills in under a light W offshore, and Sunday it doubles — 6.1ft @ 13s from 154° SSE, ~808 kJ, with a clean NW offshore in the morning. That 154° angle is the key detail: it's off dead-south, so Dee Why actually gets fed instead of being shadowed. Sunday mid-morning is your session of the week — bring the step-up. 🦈 SharkSmart's live feed is clear: no Northern Beaches shark detections in the last 24h across the drumline, drone, SLSNSW and trauma feeds.

wind.summary: Honest WNW offshore all day — 10–12 kph gusting 22–26, easing to 8 kph mid-afternoon. Clean groomed faces at every bank; the gusts put a little chop-hop in the takeoff but nothing that spoils it.

shark.summary: No shark alerts on the Northern Beaches (Palm Beach → Manly) in the last 24h. SMART drumline, DPI drone, SLSNSW and trauma feeds all read clear this morning.

days.label: Today
days.note: Small but genuinely clean. A 2.3ft @ 7s SSE windswell with a thin 15s SE groundswell under it — only ~34 kJ, so thigh-to-waist. The WNW offshore (303°) grooms every bank. Long Reef and Curl Curl hold the size; Dee Why and Manly sit soft on the SSE angle. Best window is the run off the 7:43am high before the 12:52pm low drains the banks.

swells.label: Short-period SSE windswell — the size, such as it is
Thin long-period SE groundswell — occasional better set

dee-why.window: 8:00–11:00am off the high. Clean under the WNW but underpowered — the Point is the only corner with real shape. Fun for a paddle, not a session to plan your day around.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: At 34 kJ there's nothing to push against, so sit wide on the Point and let the 15s SE lines do the work — they're the only ones with any push. Ride something with volume and keep your feet moving through the flat spots.

swells.label: SSE windswell — the magnet catches it best

long-reef.window: Pick of the four this morning. 8:00–11:00am while the WNW is straight offshore — biggest and cleanest of the coast on a SSE.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: If you're surfing today, surf here — it's a full foot bigger than Dee Why on this angle. Waist-to-chest and glassy off the offshore, so open the turns up rather than hunting a barrel that isn't there.

curl-curl.window: Second-best. 8:00–11:00am — punchy little banked peaks in the offshore, but grab it before the low fattens everything.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: The SSE angle banks the lefts here — go backhand and stay high through the soft sections. Small enough that a bit of extra foam under your chest is the difference between a wave and a paddle.

swells.label: SSE windswell — shadowed by the southern headland

manly.window: Smallest and softest of the four — clean but knee-to-waist. Not worth passing Long Reef for.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: North Steyne stays tiny on a shadowed SSE. Only worth it if you want an easy paddle on a groveller — otherwise drive north.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The throwaway day. Energy collapses to ~10 kJ — knee-to-thigh everywhere — and the W/SW builds from 16 kph to 25 kph gusting 39 by mid-afternoon. Technically offshore, but blustery and pointless. Rest day; save it for the weekend.

dee-why.window: Skip it. 10 kJ of leftover slop under a gusty W. Dawn only if you're desperate.

long-reef.window: Best of a bad bunch, which isn't saying much. Dawn patrol before the SW gets up past 20 kph, or don't bother.

curl-curl.window: Tiny and windblown by mid-morning. Not a session.

manly.window: Essentially flat. Don't waste the drive.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: The payoff, and it builds across both days. Saturday: 5.7ft @ 10s S (174°, ~425 kJ) under a light W offshore — solid but that near-dead-S angle wraps soft into Dee Why, so Long Reef and Curl Curl carry the size. Sunday is the day: 6.1ft @ 13s from 154° SSE, ~808 kJ, NW offshore in the morning swinging light N cross by midday. Longer period AND a better angle means Dee Why finally gets properly fed. Sizes below are the Sunday peak; knock roughly a foot off for Saturday.

dee-why.window: Sunday 8:00–11:00am is the session of the week — 13s SSE with a NW offshore before the N cross fills in around midday. Saturday is a foot smaller and softer on the 174° angle.

long-reef.window: Biggest of the four both days — solid overhead sets Sunday off 808 kJ. Step-up territory. Early, before the wind swings N.
alerts: Sunday runs 4–5ft with real power behind it — pick your bank and your paddle line carefully.

curl-curl.window: Punchy and well overhead on the sets Sunday — handles the size better than Dee Why but with more consequence. Dawn to mid-morning.

manly.window: Shadowed as always, which makes it the manageable option if the northern banks are too heavy. Clean but a size down.
